title: Holtec Pioneer 2 (SMR-300 at Palisades): Letter to Holtec Subject - Holtec SMR-300 Pioneer Units 1 and 2 Limited Work Authorization Application Review Schedule Update [['Letter']]

November 23, 2026


Kimberly Manzione
Executive Director, Licensing and Regulatory Affairs
Holtec International
Krishna P. Singh Technology Campus
1 Holtec Blvd., Camden, NJ 08104

SUBJECT:       HOLTEC SMR-300 PIONEER UNITS 1 AND 2 LIMITED WORK
               AUTHORIZATION APPLICATION REVIEW SCHEDULE UPDATE

Dear Ms. Manzione:

The purpose of this letter is to communicate the interim status of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) staff’s review of the limited work authorization (LWA) request for Pioneer
Units 1 and 2, including a revision to the schedule milestones for the draft safety evaluation and
draft and final environmental impact statement.

By letter dated December 31, 2025, SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades SMR, LLC, a wholly-
owned subsidiary of Holtec International (collectively, Holtec), submitted the first part of
a phased construction permit application, including an LWA request, to the NRC (Agencywide
Documents Access and Management System Accession No. ML25365A983). The LWA
application requests NRC approval to conduct certain early construction activities of a dual-unit
SMR-300 plant, Pioneer Units 1 and 2, located at the Palisades Energy Center in Covert,
Michigan, in accordance with the requirements of Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations
(10 CFR) 50.10, “License required; limited work authorization.”

On February 13, 2026, the NRC staff transmitted a letter to Holtec stating that the application
was found to be acceptable to begin a detailed technical review and provided the estimated
review schedule and resources (ML26041A223). The table below provides updated estimated
completion dates for the key review milestones:

The NRC staff issued an exemption to allow construction of permanent retaining walls prior to
LWA issuance on August 28, 2026 (91 FR 55628). The associated Environmental Assessment
and Finding of No Significant Impact was published on August 25, 2026 (91 FR 54890). By
letter dated September 29, 2026, the NRC staff notified Holtec regarding the fixed cap on
service fees associated with the NRC’s review of the Pioneer Units 1 and 2 LWA application
(ML26266A011).

Safety Review

During the regulatory audit of the safety-related portion of the application, the NRC staff
identified several areas where additional information is required in order for the staff to be able
to complete its safety review. Therefore, the staff requires additional time to review
the supplemental information and complete the Advanced Safety Evaluation Report (SER).
The NRC staff expects to complete the Advanced SER by early March 2027. The scheduled
month for Final SER completion remains unchanged, March 2027.

Environmental Review

The NRC and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Detroit District (USACE) are cooperating on
the development of an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) designed to satisfy
the environmental review obligations of both agencies. The NRC is the lead Federal agency
preparing the EIS in accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, as
amended. The USACE is a cooperating agency and will provide special expertise for activities
of the project that are under USACE’s jurisdiction.

On August 24, 2026, Holtec filed a Joint Permit Application (JPA) with the Michigan Department
of the Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE), and on August 27, 2026, Holtec provided
a copy of that filing to USACE. EGLE and USACE responded to Holtec with separate requests
for additional information (dated September 23, 2026, and November 3, 2026, respectively)
needed for the JPA to be considered administratively complete. This additional information is
also needed for the NRC and USACE staff to identify the assumptions that will be used to
complete the Draft EIS.

Because issuance of the Pioneer Units 1 and 2 EIS is dependent on the action of a third party
(i.e., USACE as a cooperating agency), it is incumbent on the applicant to adequately plan,
coordinate, or take other appropriate action to provide sufficient information in a timely manner
to complete its part of the environmental review. However, as of the date of this letter, Holtec
has not provided USACE with the additional information needed to complete the JPA, issue
a public notice, and allow its formal review to proceed. Consequently, the NRC staff anticipates
a substantial delay in completing the Draft EIS, which will, in turn, prevent the NRC from
maintaining its original estimated review schedule for the LWA.

The NRC staff is coordinating with USACE to identify the best approach for completing
the environmental review. After USACE informs the NRC of its receipt of the completed JPA
and USACE and NRC align on the appropriate path forward, the NRC staff will develop
a revised schedule for issuing the Draft EIS and Final EIS and notify Holtec of these revised
milestones via separate correspondence.

Given the recent changes to the Commission’s policy on mandatory hearings (91 FR 34661;
June 8, 2026), it is estimated that the mandatory hearing will be completed in early 2027, prior
 K. Manzione                                   3


to issuance of the Final SER and Final EIS. A decision on the LWA will be made after issuance
of the Final EIS and after completion of any potential contested hearings.

If you have any questions regarding this matter, please contact Victoria Huckabay, Senior
Project Manager, at (301) 415-5183 or by email at Victoria.Huckabay@nrc.gov. For questions
that are specific to the environmental review, please contact Robert Hoffman, Senior
Environmental Project Manager, at (301) 415-1107 or by email at Robert.Hoffman@nrc.gov.
